qs.q: A 10-year-old child presents with pharyngitis and cervical lymphadenopathy. Laboratory evaluation confirms infectious mononucleosis. Which viral family is the causative agent?
qs.e: Mononucleosis is caused by Epstein-Barr virus, which belongs to the Herpesviridae family, not picornaviruses. Picornaviruses include agents of myocarditis, hepatitis, and enteroviral meningitis.

qs.q: A 45-year-old male farmer from South America presents with chronic productive cough, cervical lymphadenopathy, and painful ulcerative lesions of the nasal mucosa. Biopsy of the mucosal lesions reveals large yeast cells with multiple peripheral buds resembling a captain's wheel. What is the primary route of acquisition for this organism?
qs.e: Paracoccidioides brasiliensis is acquired via inhalation of airborne conidia from the soil, which subsequently disseminate to produce mucocutaneous lesions. The infection is not acquired through direct skin contact or vectors.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases: MCQs

qs.q: A 55-year-old man presents with painless lymphadenopathy, and a lymph node biopsy reveals follicular lymphoma with t(14;18) translocation. Overexpression of the BCL-2 protein in this tumor promotes cell survival through which process?
qs.e: BCL-2 keeps the mitochondrial outer membrane intact, preventing cytochrome c release and blocking the intrinsic apoptotic pathway. Caspase inactivation is a different downstream process.
qs.s: Pathology by Dr. Irungu — — Oncopathology: MCQs

qs.q: What is the characteristic physical finding of lymphadenopathy typically seen in lymphoma?
qs.e: Lymphadenopathy in lymphoma is classically painless, firm, mobile, and not warm or red. Painful lymph nodes are much more suggestive of an infectious etiology.

qs.q: A 58-year-old female presents with persistent supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Her physician orders an excisional lymph node biopsy rather than fine-needle aspiration (FNA) to establish a diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. What is the primary diagnostic advantage of obtaining tissue via biopsy over FNA?
o: Preservation of architecture required for tissue classification
Higher yield of single cells required for flow cytometry analysis
Elimination of tumor cell seeding along the procedural tract
Assessment of vascular invasion into surrounding tissue structures
qs.e: Excisional or core biopsies preserve nodal tissue architecture, which is essential for differentiating architectural patterns and accurately classifying non-Hodgkin lymphoma subtypes. Fine-needle aspiration yields adequate cell suspension for flow cytometry, but lacks the structural context necessary for complete histological diagnosis.
qs.s: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma: Classification, Symptoms, Diagnosis, and: MCQs

qs.q: What imaging investigation must be performed to identify a large mediastinal mass before a lymph node biopsy in a patient with unexplained lymphadenopathy?
qs.e: Any patient with persistent, unexplained lymphadenopathy should undergo chest radiography to check for a large mediastinal mass prior to lymph node biopsy. Abdominal ultrasound would not visualize a mediastinal mass adequately.

qs.q: A 22-year-old woman is found to have mediastinal lymphadenopathy and lower cervical adenopathy. Biopsy shows fibrous bands dividing the lymphoid tissue into circumscribed nodules with lacunar cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?
qs.e: Nodular Sclerosis is the most common subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma, characterized by collagen bands dividing tissue into nodules and the presence of lacunar cells. Mixed cellularity typically lacks these prominent collagen bands and occurs more frequently in older adults.
qs.s: Hematologic Malignancies and Bleeding Disorders: MCQs

qs.q: A 55-year-old man presents with generalized lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms. Biopsy reveals numerous classic Reed-Sternberg cells within a heterogeneous inflammatory infiltrate rich in eosinophils and plasma cells, without prominent fibrosis. Which subtype is this?
qs.e: Mixed Cellularity Hodgkin lymphoma is most common in patients over 50 years old and shows plentiful classic Reed-Sternberg cells in a heterogeneous inflammatory infiltrate. Nodular sclerosis features prominent collagen bands and lacunar cells rather than being defined primarily by a mixed infiltrate without fibrosis.
qs.s: Hematologic Malignancies and Bleeding Disorders: MCQs

es.q: A 55-year-old patient of Chinese descent presents with cervical lymphadenopathy. Biopsy reveals an undifferentiated carcinoma of the nasopharynx. Discuss the primary etiological agent strongly linked to this condition and describe the characteristic histological features of the undifferentiated vari
es.m: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is strongly linked to the Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV), with the viral genome found in virtually all cases, particularly in high-incidence Chinese populations. EBV first replicates in nasopharyngeal epithelium before infecting tonsillar B lymphocytes, leading to epithelial transformation. The undifferentiated carcinoma variant, which is the most common and most closely linked to EBV, is characterized histologically by large epithelial cells with indistinct cell borders, often described as having a "syncytial" growth pattern. es.q: A 68-year-old male presents with new-onset, painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Biopsy confirms Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL). Briefly outline the primary cellular origins of NHL and their approximate percentages.
es.m: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma is a diverse group of clonal lymphoid tumors. Approximately 85% are of B-cell origin, while 15% arise from T or NK cells.

es.q: A 58-year-old patient presents with several months of unexplained fever, night sweats, and significant weight loss, alongside generalized, painless lymphadenopathy.
